title: Point-Set And CW Toolbox
notes: Open by framing the appendix as infrastructure. Later algebraic topology arguments treat cells, products, quotients, and mapping spaces as if continuity behaves automatically. This lecture explains which hypotheses make that legal, and the thumbnail strip previews the three recurring moves: cell data, retract neighborhoods, and compact-open control.

title: Toolbox Roadmap
notes: Use the roadmap as the organizing question for the whole deck. The appendix repeatedly replaces a global continuity problem by local tests: first cell closures, then products of compactly generated spaces, then mapping-space subbasic neighborhoods. The point is not memorizing propositions, but knowing which local certificate is allowed.

title: CW Construction Data
notes: Slow down the vocabulary. A cell is the open image of a disk interior, while the characteristic map remembers the whole disk and its boundary attachment. Skeleta are the successive receiving spaces. Students often blur these objects, so the figure should be read as a data diagram, not merely a picture of a space.

title: Weak Topology And Boundary Check
notes: This slide turns the CW topology into two tests. The weak topology says closedness can be checked after pulling back along characteristic maps. The matrix check says the same attaching information has an algebraic shadow: cellular boundaries compose to zero, and the tiny model has Euler characteristic one.

title: Compact Sets Become Finite
notes: Present compactness as the mechanism that turns an infinite CW complex into a finite working arena. Once a compact probe meets finitely many cells, adding all boundary faces gives a finite subcomplex. This is why many later proofs can reduce local questions to finite cellular diagrams.

title: Closure-Finiteness Can Fail
notes: The warning is that weak-looking tests are not enough. A single two-cell whose boundary meets too many zero-cells breaks closure-finiteness. The sampled drawing is finite, but the trend captures the intended obstruction: the boundary list never stabilizes into a finite cellular target.

title: Epsilon Neighborhood Retracts
notes: The collar formula is the usable content. In each cell outside the subcomplex, points move radially toward the boundary part already in the previous skeleton. With epsilon less than one, the neighborhood deformation retracts to the subcomplex and keeps the boundary fixed throughout.

title: Cellwise Continuity Scaffold
notes: This is the practical payoff of weak topology and compact generation. For maps out of a CW complex, continuity is checked on closed cells with overlap compatibility. For homotopies, the same idea is applied to each closed cell times the interval, using compact generation of products.

title: Product CW Versus Product Topology
notes: The distinction is subtle but important. The product cells always give a CW structure on the compactly generated product, while the ordinary product topology can be too coarse. In common cases, such as one locally compact factor or both factors countable, the topologies agree.

title: Dowker Wedge Witness
notes: Make the counterexample concrete through the constructed hit. The set P meets each product cell in at most one point, so the CW-closed test passes. But every ordinary product neighborhood of the wedge point contains a chosen P point; here the check records k equals 25 and t_k equals 54.

title: ENR Geometry
notes: Connect the abstract theorem to the cubical picture. Local contractibility lets maps over small cells be extended back toward K, producing a neighborhood retraction. The notebook figure uses a circle and cubical annulus as a faithful model, with radial numerical error at machine precision.

title: Domination And Mapping Telescopes
notes: Domination is a homotopy-theoretic replacement for being a literal retract. If Y maps into a CW complex X and back with r i homotopic to the identity on Y, the mapping telescope of the composite on X builds a CW model. The displayed whisker collapse is the toy mechanism.

title: Compact-Open Path Tubes
notes: This slide explains why compact-open topology is the right topology for path spaces. A basic neighborhood controls finitely many compact pieces of the domain. When the domain is compact and the target is metric, the sup metric gives the same membership test, as the saved distance check shows.

title: Evaluation, Currying, Quotients
notes: The three continuity facts are the bridge to later homotopy theory. Evaluation is continuous under local compactness, currying is equivalent to continuity of the two-variable map, and products with locally compact spaces preserve quotient maps. That is the point-set basis for loop-suspension adjunctions and quotient homotopies.

title: Hypothesis Tuner And Recap
notes: Close by turning the appendix into a decision dashboard. Compactness gives finite subcomplex control, local compactness repairs products and evaluation, weak topology permits cellwise tests, and closure-finiteness prevents pathological attachments. The applied lab values remind students that these are checkable hypotheses, not decorative assumptions.
